title: Good Fats, Bad Fats
hook: Fat isn't the enemy — the type is what matters. Swapping saturated and trans fats for unsaturated ones beats just trying to eat less fat overall.
key_points: Unsaturated fats (from fish, nuts, plant oils) are the heart-friendly ones.
Saturated fat, mostly from fatty meat and full-fat dairy, is best limited.
Trans fats are the worst for the heart and best avoided entirely.
Replace bad fats with good ones — don't just cut fat and add refined carbs.
content_html: For years the advice was simply "eat less fat," and a lot of people swapped fat for sugary, refined carbs and ended up no better off. The sharper message is about type: some fats protect your heart, others strain it, and the smart move is to trade up rather than just cut down.
extra_html: The American Heart Association groups dietary fats into three buckets. Unsaturated fats — found in fish, nuts, seeds, avocados, and plant oils like olive — are the heart-friendly ones. Saturated fat, mostly from fatty meats and full-fat dairy, is best limited. And trans fat is the worst actor of all, best avoided entirely. The crucial nuance is that cutting fat isn't the goal; replacing the harmful fats with healthier ones is. Trading butter for olive oil, or a fatty processed snack for a handful of nuts, does more for your heart than dropping fat and reaching for white bread instead. Your doctor can advise if you have specific cholesterol or heart concerns.

related.hook: High blood pressure is called the 'silent killer' for a reason — it usually has no symptoms, yet it quietly raises your risk of heart attack and stroke.

flashcards.prompt: Which types of fat are the heart-friendly ones, and which to limit?
flashcards.back_html: Unsaturated fats (fish, nuts, seeds, plant oils) are the heart-friendly ones. Saturated fat is best limited, and trans fat is best avoided entirely. The key move is to replace the bad with the good, not just cut fat.

flashcards.prompt: What's the best move for heart health when it comes to fats?

choices.text: Replace saturated and trans fats with unsaturated fats
Cut all fat from your diet completely
Swap fats for extra refined sugar and white bread

flashcards.explanation_html: The American Heart Association advises replacing saturated and trans fats with unsaturated fats — not eliminating fat, and not trading it for refined carbs.

flashcards.prompt: Which fat is considered the worst for heart health?
flashcards.explanation_html: The AHA singles out trans fat as the most harmful to the heart and recommends avoiding it.
